title: Characterizing Cell Migration Within Three-dimensional In Vitro Wound Environments
protocol: Warm filtered Dulbecco's Modified Eagle's Medium (DMEM), fetal bovine serum (FBS), L-glutamine, and penicillin/streptomycin in a 37 °C water bath.
Prepare neonatal human dermal fibroblast (HDFn) media by supplementing warmed DMEM with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 1% L-glutamine.
Thaw a vial of frozen HDFns in a biological safety cabinet.
Centrifuge the thawed cells for 8 min at 200 x g to remove cryopreservation medium.
Resuspend cells in prepared HDFn media at a density of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Seed resuspended cells into a T-75 culture flask.
Place the seeded flask in an incubator (37 °C, 5% CO2) for cell proliferation.
Store HDFn media at 4 °C.
Prepare pro- and anti-migratory reagents as needed.
When cells reach 80% confluency, aspirate the media.
Add 5 mL of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to the flask.
Store the flask in a 37 °C incubator for 5 min to fully detach cells from the flask surface.
Add 5 mL of warmed media to the flask to neutralize the trypsin.
In a microcentrifuge tube, mix 10 μL of Trypan Blue and 10 μL of the cell suspension.
Centrifuge the original cell suspension for 8 min at 200 x g.
While the cell suspension is being centrifuged, add 10 μL of the Trypan Blue cell suspension to a hemocytometer.
Perform a cell count using the hemocytometer.
Following centrifugation, aspirate media without dislodging the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet at a concentration of 1.25 x 10^5 cells/mL.
Add 5 mL of sterile phosphate buffered saline (PBS) to the bottom of a 10 cm Petri dish.
Invert the lid of the Petri dish.
Add several 20 μL drops of the cell suspension onto the inner surface of the Petri dish lid.
Quickly invert the lid and place it back on the bottom of the dish carefully.
Place the dish in a 37 °C incubator to allow spheroids to grow for a period of 72 h.
Perform embedding of spheroids into 3D matrix in a culture hood.
Create a clot solution of sufficient volume to add 100 μL per well.
Clots are comprised of 10% 10X HEPES buffer by volume, 2 mg/mL human fibrinogen, and 0.1 U/mL human alpha thrombin.
Add thrombin last and quickly add solution to desired wells in a 48-well plate to prevent clots from polymerizing prior to addition.
Gently shake/tap well plate to ensure fibrin clot mixture coats entire well.
Place well plate in incubator for 1 hour to allow bottom clot layer to polymerize.
Transfer spheroids to the fibrin layer.
Remove well plate and Petri dish containing spheroids from incubator.
Examine spheroids under a microscope.
Invert lid of Petri dish to access hanging drop cultures.
Attach 21 G needle to 1 mL syringe.
Carefully transfer one drop from inverted lid into center of each well, avoiding puncture of polymerized fibrin layer.
Slowly pull the drop into the needle until it is fully inside; stop pulling as soon as entire drop is inside.
Examine well plate under a microscope to ensure spheroids have properly transferred.
Create another clot solution for the second fibrin layer using the same preparation as the first fibrin layer.
Carefully pipette 100 μl of the new clot solution onto each spheroid-containing drop and examine under a microscope to ensure spheroids are still intact.
Return the well plate to the incubator and allow the second layer to polymerize for 1 hour.
Warm HDFn media to 37°C.
Prepare media for each group including appropriate concentrations of pro/anti-migratory agents to be evaluated.
Remove the well plate from the incubator and place in a culture hood.
Add 500 μl of standard media to each well of the control spheroid group.
Add 500 μl of inhibitory media to each well of the migration-inhibited spheroid group.
Add 500 μl of pro-migratory media to each well of the migration-enhanced spheroid group.
Return the well plate to the incubator.
Change media every 48 hours.
Image spheroids using brightfield microscopy immediately after addition of media (0 h).
Repeat imaging every 24 hours for a total of 72 hours.
Optionally, take z-stack images at each time point to assess migration in different planes.
Use ImageJ to analyze cell outgrowth by tracing the border of each spheroid at successive time points.
Determine percent increase in area for each spheroid using the "Measure" function in ImageJ.
